title: Security Trading Policy

tiers.name: Restricted Persons
tiers.description: The Board (Directors); employees and officers of Propel Investments Pty Limited (the Manager) while the Management Agreement dated 11 September 2017 is in force; employees of the Company who work out of the Manager's office while that agreement is in force; and the Company Secretary. Subject to closed periods, prior notification of dealings, and the overriding Inside Information ban.

tiers.name: Directors
tiers.description: Members of the Board; distinguished only for the duty to file ASX substantial shareholding notices under section 205G of the Corporations Act.

tiers.name: Associated Party
tiers.description: A Restricted Person's immediate family (including a spouse or equivalent, or dependent), family company or trust, which must comply with the same restrictions as apply to the Restricted Person.

windows.end_anchor: close of trading on the business day after the Company's half yearly results are announced to the ASX
close of trading on the business day after the Company's annual results are announced to the ASX

rules.detail: The Securities definition (Corporations Act s92, plus shares/options/debentures of the Company) does not extend to third-party derivative products, and clause 1.9(a) expressly states there is currently no restriction on Restricted Persons entering into hedging arrangements, which would include an OTC put/call collar. Subject to the overriding Inside Information ban and the Board's reserved right to introduce restrictions in future.
rules.evidence: Although the Board may introduce restrictions in the future, there is no restrictions on: (a) Restricted Persons entering into hedging arrangements

rules.detail: Express, current-state permission for hedging arrangements over Company securities; no unvested equity plan or holding-lock concept appears elsewhere in this Policy. Subject only to the overriding Inside Information ban and the Board's reserved right to restrict in future.
rules.evidence: Although the Board may introduce restrictions in the future, there is no restrictions on: (a) Restricted Persons entering into hedging arrangements

rules.detail: Monetisation is not named, but a prepaid forward or similar arrangement is economically a hedging arrangement, so it falls within the express permission in 1.9(a) rather than being separately restricted.
rules.evidence: Although the Board may introduce restrictions in the future, there is no restrictions on: (a) Restricted Persons entering into hedging arrangements

rules.detail: Short selling is not named or defined anywhere in the Policy.
Securities lending is not mentioned anywhere in the Policy.

CFDs are not named. If entered as a hedge of the Company's securities they fall within the express permission for hedging arrangements in 1.9(a); the Policy has no separate short-term or speculative dealing restriction that would otherwise catch a CFD.
rules.evidence: Although the Board may introduce restrictions in the future, there is no restrictions on: (a) Restricted Persons entering into hedging arrangements

rules.detail: Express, current-state permission to include Company securities in a margin loan portfolio or otherwise deal in them pursuant to a margin lending arrangement, subject only to the overriding Inside Information ban and the Board's reserved right to restrict in future.
rules.evidence: there is no restrictions on: ... (b) Restricted Persons including his or her securities in the Company in margin loan portfolio or otherwise deal in securities of the Company pursuant to a margin lending arrangement

rules.detail: General encumbrance is not separately named, but the express permission for margin loan arrangements (which necessarily involve granting security over the shares) indicates encumbering Company securities is not otherwise restricted by this Policy.
rules.evidence: Restricted Persons including his or her securities in the Company in margin loan portfolio or otherwise deal in securities of the Company pursuant to a margin lending arrangement

rules.detail: Only margin lending is expressly named as unrestricted; other secured financing structures (e.g. a bespoke loan secured by pledge) are not separately addressed, but nothing else in the Policy restricts them either.
rules.evidence: there is no restrictions on: ... (b) Restricted Persons including his or her securities in the Company in margin loan portfolio or otherwise deal in securities of the Company pursuant to a margin lending arrangement

rules.detail: There is no short-term or speculative dealing restriction anywhere in this Policy.

clearance.evidence: Restricted Persons are required to notify the Company of intended dealings in the Company's securities, by themselves or their associated parties, prior to such intended dealings ... The Company Secretary will confer with the chairperson of the Board (Chairperson) in relation to any proposed dealing.

undertakings or elections to take up entitlements under a rights issue or other offer (including an offer of shares in lieu of a cash dividend); the take up of entitlements under a rights issue or other offer; allowing entitlements to lapse; the sale of sufficient entitlements to allow take up of the balance of the entitlements under a rights issue
the take up of shares pursuant to a dividend reinvestment plan
undertakings to accept, or the acceptance of, a takeover offer or pursuant to a scheme of arrangement implemented in accordance with section 411 of the Corporations Act
the purchase of shares or the communication of information pursuant to a requirement imposed by law
bona fide gifts to a Director by a third party
transfers of securities in the Company already held into a superannuation fund or other saving scheme in which the Restricted Person is a beneficiary

trading under an offer or invitation made to all or most of the security holders, such as, a rights issue, a security purchase plan, a dividend or distribution reinvestment plan and an equal access buy-back

exemption_authority: The Chairperson (or the other Directors where the Chairperson is involved) may, in exceptional circumstances and where it is the only reasonable course of action, grant written clearance for a Restricted Person to sell (not purchase) shares when otherwise prohibited, for severe financial hardship, a court order or enforceable undertaking, another overriding legal/regulatory requirement, or other circumstances the Chairperson deems exceptional; clearance cannot be given while there is a matter about which there is inside information, and the clearance must specify its maximum duration in writing.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Although the Board may introduce restrictions in the future, there is no restrictions on: (a) Restricted Persons entering into hedging arrangements
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: An equity collar (purchased put and written call) over the Restricted Person's Propel shares is a hedging arrangement expressly unrestricted under the current Policy, subject only to the overriding Inside Information ban; the Board's express reservation of a future right to restrict hedging means the bank should obtain fresh confirmation for each transaction and consider a policy-change trigger in its documentation.

bespoke_clauses.clause: there is no restrictions on: ... (b) Restricted Persons including his or her securities in the Company in margin loan portfolio or otherwise deal in securities of the Company pursuant to a margin lending arrangement
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The loan leg of a funded collar, secured on the collared shares, faces no policy-based bar since margin lending and related secured dealing in Company securities is expressly unrestricted; again this is the Board's current position only and could change.

bespoke_clauses.topic: notification scope unclear for hedge/loan legs
bespoke_clauses.clause: Restricted Persons are required to notify the Company of intended dealings in the Company's securities ... prior to such intended dealings.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: It is unclear whether entering the collar or margin/secured loan itself (as opposed to any on-market dealing in the underlying shares) falls within the notification duty, given clause 1.9 treats hedging and margin lending as outside the Policy's restrictions; the bank should seek written confirmation from the Company Secretary or Chairperson on whether notification is expected.

bespoke_clauses.clause: The Policy contains no clause restricting short-term or speculative dealing.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Unlike most ASX trading policies, there is no minimum holding period or tenor restriction that would constrain how quickly a collar could be entered, unwound or rolled.

summary: This Policy is unusually favourable to a funded collar: clause 1.9 expressly states that there is currently no restriction on Restricted Persons entering into hedging arrangements or on including their Propel shares in a margin loan portfolio or otherwise dealing in Company securities pursuant to a margin lending arrangement, so both the derivative legs and the loan leg secured on the collared shares face no policy-based bar. The main constraint is the overriding Inside Information ban, which applies to any dealing at any time, and the two closed periods (1 January to the day after half-year results; 1 July to the day after annual results), though it is unclear whether entering the derivative or loan legs (as distinct from on-market share dealing) is caught by the closed period or the clause 1.5 pre-dealing notification duty, so written confirmation from the Company Secretary or Chairperson is advisable before executing. There is no short-term or speculative dealing restriction at all, so collar tenor is unconstrained by this Policy. The permissive position on hedging and margin lending is expressly stated to be the Board's current position only, and the Board may introduce restrictions in future, so the bank's documentation should anticipate the possibility of a policy change during the life of the facility. Overall, a funded collar appears fully permitted on the current wording, subject to the Insider Trading Policy and confirming the notification position with the Company Secretary.
